newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul mulls early expansion of foreign stock limit.
newsitem.headline: Seoul mulls early expansion of foreign stock limit.

text.p: The South Korean government is considering various measures to slow the local currency"s sharp fall against the dollar, including an earlier than scheduled expansion of the foreign stock holding limit, a finance and economic ministry official said on Tuesday.
The official described the recent won/dollar rate as "abnormal", and said the government should not stand idle any longer. The won hit an 84-month low of 887.00 in early morning trading.
"If we continue to leave the current situation alone, we would be neglecting our duty," he added. "We are considering various measures to improve the situation."

He said the steps would be strong and diverse, and may include an earlier than scheduled expansion of the foreign stock holding ceiling and tax-exemption for capital gains by Japanese investment funds. But he declined to give further details.
South Korea had earlier said it would raise the foreign stock ownership ceiling to 23 percent this year from the current 20 percent, and by a further three percentage points in 1998 and 1999.
The news sparked a rebound in the won to 869.40 in the afternoon session.
In the morning session, a senior Bank of Korea official also said the central bank would take "strong measures which are different from the past" to stabilise the won's fall.
